user.title: Functions Board
user.description:
Adds a Functions page to the sidebar for administrators: one whiteboard per function, showing its automations, scripts, helpers and devices wired together.

It starts in Organise only mode. A function is a Home Assistant label; the board adds and removes labels and categories, and Pause turns a function's automations off until you resume them. It doesn't create, edit or delete your automations, scripts or helpers.

In the integration's options you can switch to Full manager, which also creates and deletes automations, scripts, helpers and functions, edits the wiring in automation and script configs, and runs test changes. The board shows every change before it happens, and you can undo everything except test changes.

abort.single_instance_allowed: Functions Board is already set up.

data.card: Make the Functions card available on dashboards

data_description.mode: Organise only: labels, categories, and Pause and Resume. Full manager adds: creating and deleting automations, scripts, helpers and functions; editing the wiring in automation and script configs, which rewrites automations.yaml and scripts.yaml the way Home Assistant's own editors do (YAML comments are lost); and test changes such as simulated states, fired events and test runs. Every change is shown before it happens; all but test changes can be undone.
data_description.card: Loads the board on dashboard pages so you can add a custom:functions-board card without adding a resource by hand.
data_description.nodered_url: Lets Home Assistant read your Node-RED flows itself, so the board shows them on every device without opening Node-RED first. For the Node-RED app, turn on its direct access port (Network, 1880 by default) and enter http://127.0.0.1:1880 (https:// if the app has SSL on). Leave empty to read the flows only through the Node-RED page Home Assistant opens for you. Flows are still read only while Node-RED flows is switched on in a board's Key.
data_description.nodered_username: For the Node-RED app: a Home Assistant user's username (a separate, non-administrator user just for this is best). For another Node-RED: a user from its adminAuth; read permission is enough.
data_description.nodered_password: Kept in the integration's settings. Leave empty to keep the one already set.

error.invalid_url: Enter an address starting with http:// or https://.
error.nodered_cannot_connect: Couldn't reach Node-RED at that address. For the Node-RED app, check that its direct access port is set in its Network settings.
error.nodered_invalid_auth: Node-RED refused the username or password.
error.nodered_unexpected: Node-RED answered, but not with its flows. Check the address.
